data.question_intent: Inquire about capital ratio, restructuring charges, and future expectations
data.question_quote: I was surprised that the capital ratio wasn't stronger, given the earnings beat and risk-weighted assets falling. I just wondered if you could give us some more colour around 'Other' movements - I think it was a minus-40-basis-point hit in the chart - exactly what's driving that and how we might expect that to progress going forward.
data.answer_quote: On restructuring charges, we're not changing our full-year guidance we gave at full-year results. You're right: Q1 was unusually low, so yes, you should expect those to pick up as the year progresses. On capital, a few things: there were deductions for fair value reserve movements on cash flow and negative FX movements. There was a higher deduction for BoCom as its profits increased and, again, note that we talk about a 10-basis-point deduction for the foreseeable dividend, which is new for us, but represents a change in policy because we've shifted to a payout-ratio policy.
data.reason: The answer directly addresses the capital ratio and restructuring charges, providing specific reasons for the observed figures and future expectations, aligning with the question's intent.
